Using `slurmworkflow` with EpiModel

2026-10-12

Source: vignettes/epimodelhiv-slurmworkflow.Rmd
epimodelhiv-slurmworkflow.Rmd

Introduction

slurmworkflow builds workflows for a SLURM equipped high-performance computing (HPC) cluster. A workflow is a sequence of steps, each one a SLURM job, that run one after the other on the HPC. We build the workflow on our own computer, copy it to the HPC, and start it there with a single command.

This vignette explains the ideas behind the workflows we use in applied EpiModelHIV projects. It follows the EpiModelHIV-Template (branch v3.3.x) and uses the Rollins School of Public Health (RSPH) HPC at Emory University as the example cluster. It is not a step-by-step guide. For that, follow the README in each chapter of the Template and the wiki page Running Project Workflows on the HPC.

The Template uses renv and needs access to the private EpiModelHIV-p repository. We assume that the project is a git repository cloned both on your computer and on the HPC.

Structure of an applied EpiModelHIV project

All the R code lives under R/:

  • R/00-setup.R: one-time setup of the project library with renv.
  • R/shared_variables.R: paths, time steps and other values shared by every script. The paths to generated files point inside data/run/: for example est_dir is data/run/estimates/ and scenarios_dir is data/run/scenarios/.
  • R/hpc_configs.R: the HPC settings and the make_em_workflow() function used by every workflow.
  • R/netsim_settings.R: builds the param and init objects and the path_to_est and path_to_restart paths used by the simulations.
  • One folder per chapter: R/A-networks, R/B-model_dev, R/C-calibration and R/D-interventions. Each chapter has a README, numbered scripts (1-estimation.R, 2-diagnostics.R, …) to run locally in order, workflow-*.R scripts that build HPC workflows, and a z-context.R file that switches between local and HPC settings.

The data/ folder contains:

  • data/input/: files the project needs before any code runs, such as model parameters and scenario definitions. Tracked by git.
  • data/run/: everything the code produces: network estimates, calibration and scenario runs. Not tracked by git.
  • data/output/: final tables and figures. Not tracked by git.

The project has two renv lockfiles. renv.lock records the full local environment, analysis packages included. renv.lock.hpc records only what the model needs on the HPC: EpiModelHIV, EpiModelHPC, ARTnetData and their dependencies. Workflows are built in workflows/, which is not tracked by git either.

Two per-user values go in the project .Renviron file (open it with usethis::edit_r_environ("project")): EPIMODELHIV_DIR, the path to your local clone of EpiModelHIV-p, and HPC_MAIL_USER, the address SLURM mails about your jobs.

Local and HPC contexts

Every numbered script and every workflow sources R/shared_variables.R and the z-context.R file of its chapter. z-context.R looks for a variable named hpc_context. When it is TRUE, it sets context <- "hpc" and the full-scale settings; otherwise it sets context <- "local" and small, fast ones. In R/A-networks/z-context.R, for example, the local context estimates 10,000-node networks with the Stochastic-Approximation method on one core, and the HPC context estimates 100,000-node networks with MCMLE on 10 cores.

The context also goes into the file names, so local and HPC results never overwrite each other: the network estimates are saved as data/run/estimates/netest-local.rds or data/run/estimates/netest-hpc.rds.

On the HPC, workflow steps run the same numbered scripts with hpc_context = TRUE. The goal is that a script that runs locally also runs on the HPC without modification, so test every script locally first.

Note: run each numbered script in a fresh R session (Ctrl+Shift+F10 in RStudio) to avoid starting from a polluted environment, which makes debugging very hard. Do not use rm(list = ls()) instead: it does not do the same thing. It also breaks the scripts run by step_tmpl_do_call_script(), because it deletes the variables the step defines before running the script.

Workflows and steps

A workflow is a folder, workflows/<name>/, holding a start_workflow.sh script and one subfolder per step. Each workflow-*.R script builds one workflow in two moves:

  1. make_em_workflow() creates the workflow and its first step, which brings the project on the HPC up to date (see below).
  2. Each call to slurmworkflow::add_workflow_step() appends a step. Its step_tmpl argument is a step template, which says what the step runs, and its sbatch_opts argument says which resources the step asks SLURM for.

sbatch_opts accepts any long-form sbatch option without the leading -- (“cpus-per-task” is valid, “c” is not). The options given to the workflow when it is created are the defaults for every step, and each step can override them.

The steps are chained by a small controller job, so step 2 starts when step 1 is over, and so on. A step can also change which step runs next; this is how swfcalib loops over calibration iterations.

The templates used in the Template come from two packages:

  • slurmworkflow: step_tmpl_do_call_script() runs an R script that is on the HPC, step_tmpl_do_call() runs an R function, and step_tmpl_map() runs a function over many inputs as a SLURM array.
  • EpiModelHPC: step_tmpl_renv_restore() updates the project, step_tmpl_netsim_scenarios() runs scenario simulations, step_tmpl_merge_netsim_scenarios_tibble() merges their output, and step_tmpl_netsim_swfcalib_output() runs the model with calibrated parameters.

make_em_workflow(): the common first step

Every workflow in the Template starts with make_em_workflow(), defined in R/hpc_configs.R. Here is a slightly shortened version:

current_git_branch <- "main"          # <- USER: your git branch

hpc_node_setup <- c(
  ". /projects/epimodel/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh",
  "spack unload -a",
  "spack load r@4.5.1"
)

make_em_workflow <- function(wf_name, override = FALSE, update_renv = TRUE) {
  # The Template stops with instructions if this is not set in `.Renviron`
  hpc_mail_user <- Sys.getenv("HPC_MAIL_USER")

  if (update_renv) {
    renv::snapshot(
      packages = c("EpiModelHIV", "EpiModelHPC", "ARTnetData"),
      lockfile = "renv.lock.hpc",
      prompt = FALSE
    )
  }

  wf_path <- paste0("workflows/", wf_name)
  if (override && fs::dir_exists(wf_path)) fs::dir_delete(wf_path)

  wf <- slurmworkflow::create_workflow(
    wf_name = wf_name,
    default_sbatch_opts = list(
      "partition" =
        "epimodel,short-cpu,day-long-cpu,week-long-cpu,month-long-cpu",
      "mail-type" = "FAIL",
      "mail-user" = hpc_mail_user
    )
  )

  # Update renv on the HPC
  wf <- slurmworkflow::add_workflow_step(
    wf_summary = wf,
    step_tmpl = EpiModelHPC::step_tmpl_renv_restore(
      git_branch = current_git_branch,
      setup_lines = hpc_node_setup,
      lockfile = if (update_renv) "renv.lock.hpc" else NULL
    ),
    sbatch_opts = list(
      "mem" = "16G",
      "cpus-per-task" = 4,
      "time" = 180
    )
  )

  wf
}

It does four things.

It refreshes renv.lock.hpc from the packages installed in your local project library. Install the EpiModelHIV-p version you want to run locally first, then build the workflow, then commit and push renv.lock.hpc.

It creates the workflow in workflows/<wf_name>/. create_workflow() stops if that folder already exists; override = TRUE deletes the old one first.

It sets the default sbatch options: mail HPC_MAIL_USER when a step fails, and run on any of the listed partitions. SLURM starts each job on whichever listed partition can run it first, and it considers the lab’s dedicated epimodel partition (15 nodes, no time limit) before the shared ones: short-cpu (8 hours), day-long-cpu (1 day), week-long-cpu (7 days) and month-long-cpu (31 days). A step that asks for more time than a partition allows only runs on the others. Lab members can also add CIDMATH, 8 dedicated nodes shared with three other groups. The preemptable partition that older projects used no longer exists. interactive-cpu (12 hours, at most 16 cores per job) is meant for srun sessions and largemem holds high-memory nodes; neither is needed for routine runs.

It adds the restore step, which is always step 1. On a compute node, this step loads R with hpc_node_setup, checks that the HPC clone is on current_git_branch (and stops otherwise, to avoid running the wrong code), runs git pull, and restores the packages listed in renv.lock.hpc. This is how EpiModelHIV-p and the other packages get installed on the HPC: there is no need to run renv::init() or renv::restore() by hand. Do not run them on the login node either. The login node runs a different release of the operating system than the compute nodes, so renv keeps a separate library for it that the jobs never use.

hpc_node_setup holds the bash lines that make R available in each step. On RSPH, R comes from spack: r@4.6.1 is the current build and r@4.5.1 is still available. Load the version recorded in your lockfile, and always give the full version: spack load r@4.3, for example, fails because it matches several builds.

Outside the Template: swf_configs_rsph()

Projects that do not use make_em_workflow() can get the same settings from swf_configs_rsph():

library(slurmworkflow)
library(EpiModelHPC)

hpc_configs <- swf_configs_rsph(
  partition = c("epimodel", "short-cpu", "day-long-cpu"),
  r_version = "4.6.1",
  mail_user = "<netid>@emory.edu"
)

wf <- create_workflow(
  wf_name = "my_workflow",
  default_sbatch_opts = hpc_configs$default_sbatch_opts
)

wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf_summary = wf,
  step_tmpl = step_tmpl_renv_restore(
    git_branch = "main",
    setup_lines = hpc_configs$r_loader
  ),
  sbatch_opts = hpc_configs$renv_sbatch_opts
)

hpc_configs holds:

  • default_sbatch_opts: the partition list and the mail settings.
  • renv_sbatch_opts: the resources for the restore step.
  • r_loader: the spack lines, followed by a trap that stops a job’s own R workers when the job is canceled or times out (see ?swf_cleanup_r_workers). Pass it as setup_lines to every step template.
  • max_cores: the most CPUs one task can request on every listed partition.

See ?swf_configs_rsph for the partitions it accepts and their limits. swf_configs_hyak() does the same for the HYAK cluster at the University of Washington.

Example: estimating the networks

R/A-networks/workflow-networks.R runs the network estimation and diagnostics at full scale. Estimating 100,000-node networks with MCMLE would take days on a laptop.

library(slurmworkflow)

hpc_context <- TRUE
source("R/shared_variables.R", local = TRUE)
source("R/A-networks/z-context.R", local = TRUE)
source("R/hpc_configs.R", local = TRUE)

wf <- make_em_workflow("networks", override = TRUE)

wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf_summary = wf,
  step_tmpl = step_tmpl_do_call_script(
    r_script = "R/A-networks/1-estimation.R",
    args = list(hpc_context = TRUE),
    setup_lines = hpc_node_setup
  ),
  sbatch_opts = list(
    "cpus-per-task" = est_cores,
    "time" = "24:00:00",
    "mem" = "0"
  )
)

wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf_summary = wf,
  step_tmpl = step_tmpl_do_call_script(
    r_script = "R/A-networks/2-diagnostics.R",
    args = list(hpc_context = TRUE),
    setup_lines = hpc_node_setup
  ),
  sbatch_opts = list(
    "mail-type" = "END",
    "cpus-per-task" = est_cores,
    "time" = "24:00:00",
    "mem" = "0"
  )
)

Setting hpc_context <- TRUE before sourcing z-context.R gives us the HPC settings in this script too, including est_cores (10).

step_tmpl_do_call_script() runs a script that is already on the HPC, in the git clone of the project, after defining the variables listed in args. The syntax is similar to base::do.call(). Here the scripts start with hpc_context = TRUE, so they pick the HPC settings when they source z-context.R.

The sbatch_opts of these two steps ask for est_cores CPUs, 24 hours, and mem = "0", which means all the memory of the node. That reserves a whole node, which network estimation needs; do not use it for simulation steps. With 24 hours, these steps cannot run on short-cpu. The last step asks for a mail when it ends, so we know when the workflow is done.

The steps write netest-hpc.rds, netstats-hpc.rds and epistats-hpc.rds to data/run/estimates/ on the HPC, and the diagnostics to data/run/diagnostics/. Once they are downloaded to the same folders locally, R/A-networks/3-assess.R reads them (see the chapter README).

Example: running intervention scenarios

R/D-interventions/workflow-intervention.R runs every scenario in data/input/scenarios.csv many times, starting from the restart point made in the calibration chapter (data/run/estimates/restart-hpc.rds), then merges and processes the results.

Simulation step

Terminology:

  • simulation: one run of an epidemic model.
  • scenario: a set of parameter values for a simulation. See vignette("model-parameters", package = "EpiModel").
  • batch: a set of up to n_cores simulations of the same scenario, run in parallel by one SLURM task.
library(slurmworkflow)
library(EpiModelHPC)
library(EpiModelHIV)

hpc_context <- TRUE
source("R/shared_variables.R", local = TRUE)
source("R/D-interventions/z-context.R", local = TRUE)
source("R/hpc_configs.R", local = TRUE)

max_cores <- 8

source("R/netsim_settings.R", local = TRUE) # `param`, `init`, `path_to_restart`

control <- control_msm(
  start          = restart_time,
  nsteps         = intervention_end,
  initialize.FUN = reinit_msm,
  verbose        = FALSE
)

wf <- make_em_workflow("interventions", override = TRUE)

scenarios_df <- read.csv("data/input/scenarios.csv")
scenarios_list <- EpiModel::create_scenario_list(scenarios_df)

wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf_summary = wf,
  step_tmpl = step_tmpl_netsim_scenarios(
    path_to_restart, param, init, control,
    scenarios_list = scenarios_list,
    output_dir = scenarios_dir,
    n_rep = 32,
    n_cores = max_cores,
    max_array_size = 1000,
    setup_lines = hpc_node_setup
  ),
  sbatch_opts = list(
    "mail-type" = "FAIL,TIME_LIMIT",
    "cpus-per-task" = max_cores,
    "time" = "04:00:00",
    "mem-per-cpu" = "5G"
  )
)

These simulations restart from a previous simulation rather than from time 0, so control sets start = restart_time and initialize.FUN = reinit_msm, a function from EpiModelHIV-p that handles the restart.

step_tmpl_netsim_scenarios() takes the same arguments as netsim_scenarios(), which runs the same thing locally:

  • path_to_restart, param, init and control: the inputs to netsim(). The first one is the path to the restart point on the HPC, which netsim() uses as its x argument. The nsims and ncores values in control are replaced by the step.
  • scenarios_list: the scenarios made by EpiModel::create_scenario_list().
  • output_dir: where to save the simulations, here data/run/scenarios/.
  • n_rep: how many times to run each scenario. 32 is enough to test the workflow; final analyses use many more.
  • n_cores: how many simulations each task runs in parallel, on as many CPUs.
  • max_array_size: the most tasks submitted at once (see below).
  • setup_lines: the bash lines that load R.

Each scenario is run in ceiling(n_rep / n_cores) batches, and each batch is one task of a SLURM array. With n_rep = 32 and n_cores = 8, each scenario takes 4 batches, so 10 scenarios make an array of 40 tasks. When n_rep is not a multiple of n_cores, the last batch of each scenario runs the remainder. Each batch is saved as sim__<scenario id>__<batch number>.rds in output_dir. Files from an earlier run are not deleted, so empty data/run/scenarios/ on the HPC before running new scenarios.

RSPH sets SLURM’s MaxArraySize to 1001, so one array holds at most 1001 tasks (indices 0 to 1000), and we use max_array_size = 1000. When a step has more tasks than max_array_size, slurmworkflow splits it into parts of at most that size and submits each part when the previous one is over. With 3,000 tasks, max_array_size = 1000 makes 3 parts. Older projects use 500, which works but can double the number of parts.

Each task asks for 8 CPUs for 4 hours, with 5 GB of memory per CPU. RSPH does not enforce memory requests, so ask for what the simulations really use: a task that uses more than it asked for is not stopped and slows down the other jobs on its node. Tasks of 8 cores fit on partly busy nodes and usually start sooner than whole-node tasks. The task mails us if it fails or runs out of time.

control_msm() keeps the final state of the model in each saved simulation (save.run = TRUE). On a 100,000-node model this state is most of the file. When the simulations are only read through merged tibbles, as here, save.run = FALSE makes the files much smaller. Keep the default when a restart point will be picked from the files, as in the calibration chapter.

Merging and processing steps 

wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf_summary = wf,
  step_tmpl = step_tmpl_merge_netsim_scenarios_tibble(
    sim_dir = scenarios_dir,
    output_dir = fs::path(scenarios_dir, "merged_tibbles"),
    steps_to_keep = intervention_end - intervention_start,
    cols = dplyr::everything(),
    n_cores = max_cores,
    setup_lines = hpc_node_setup
  ),
  sbatch_opts = list(
    "cpus-per-task" = max_cores,
    "time" = "02:00:00",
    "mem-per-cpu" = "5G"
  )
)

wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf_summary = wf,
  step_tmpl = step_tmpl_do_call_script(
    r_script = "R/D-interventions/3-process_tables.R",
    args = list(hpc_context = TRUE),
    setup_lines = hpc_node_setup
  ),
  sbatch_opts = list(
    "cpus-per-task" = max_cores,
    "time" = "04:00:00",
    "mem-per-cpu" = "5G"
  )
)

step_tmpl_merge_netsim_scenarios_tibble() turns all the batches of a scenario into a single tibble, saved as df__<scenario id>.rds in output_dir. It keeps only the last steps_to_keep time steps and the columns selected by cols (batch_number, sim and time are always kept). These files are much smaller than the raw simulations and are what we download.

The processing scripts then run on the HPC with step_tmpl_do_call_script(), as in the networks workflow. The Template adds a last step for the plots, with "mail-type" = "END" so that we get a mail when the workflow is done.

Running a workflow on the HPC

The wiki page Running Project Workflows on the HPC gives the commands. These are the ideas behind them.

Two channels. The code and renv.lock.hpc reach the HPC through git: commit and push them, and the restore step pulls them. The workflow folder is not tracked by git, so copy it with scp -r into the workflows/ folder of the project on the HPC (for example /projects/epimodel/<netid>/<project>/workflows/). Files in data/run/ that a run reads but that were made locally, such as a restart point, must be copied with scp as well. A file that is neither pushed nor copied does not exist on the HPC.

Start from the project folder. On the HPC, go to the root of the project (where renv.lock.hpc is) and run ./workflows/<name>/start_workflow.sh. The script must be executed, not sourced. Every step runs in the folder the workflow was started from, which is why the relative paths such as data/run/ work. start_workflow.sh -s <n> starts the workflow at step n, and start_workflow.sh -h lists the other options.

Follow the jobs. SLURM mails HPC_MAIL_USER when a step fails and when the last step ends. squeue -u $USER lists your pending and running jobs; the steps of a workflow are named <workflow name>_step<n>. The output of each step, and of each array task, goes to a file in workflows/<name>/log/ on the HPC. sacct and seff do not work on RSPH because SLURM accounting is turned off. To stop a workflow, cancel its jobs by name (scancel -u $USER --name=<workflow name>_step<n>) rather than all of your jobs at once.

Download the results. The outputs are in the data/run/ folder of the project on the HPC. Copy what you need with scp to the same path in your local project, preferably merged tibbles and summaries rather than raw simulation files.

Calibration with swfcalib

Automated calibration uses the same building blocks. R/C-calibration/workflow-swfcalib.R in the Template chains swfcalib::calibration_step1(), calibration_step2() and calibration_step3() with step_tmpl_do_call() and step_tmpl_map(), and then runs the calibrated model with step_tmpl_netsim_swfcalib_output(). See the swfcalib vignette and R/C-calibration/README.md in the Template.

Other helpers

add_doctor_register_step() and add_doctor_teardown_step() connect a workflow to the deploy doctor, a separate SLURM job that watches for stalled tasks and requeues them. See their help pages and hpc_doctor_script().
